title: Load a caulking gun and seal the joint between a bath and its tiles
instruction: Load the caulking gun, seal the joint between the bath and the tiles, and put the gun down.
context: Resealing the joint between a bath and its tiles is one of the commonest home repairs, done by householders as well as decorators and handymen. The gun has to be loaded (its rod comes back only while the release is held), and the bead only seals if the trigger meters enough silicone while the nozzle runs along the corner, so that it is unbroken and wets both the rim and the tiles.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) An empty steel skeleton caulking gun for 310 ml cartridges (0.57 kg in all), lying level along the table, nozzle end to the left, its cradle's axis 30 cm forward and 9 cm above the table: a red powder-coated steel frame (0.36 kg) with an open half-round cradle 5.6 cm across and 23.6 cm long, from a back plate 2 cm left of the centre line to a front yoke 25.6 cm left with a V notch for the nozzle; behind the cradle a drive housing 7 cm long, and under its back a black rubber pistol grip 2.4 by 2.8 cm with a flared butt, its foot on the table; the front of the cradle rests on a pine rest block 6 cm wide, 4 cm long and 6 cm tall. (2) The gun's red pressed-steel trigger (70 g), hinged 3 cm below the rod, its 5 cm blade leaning forward in front of the grip with a rounded finger rest 3.6 cm below the pivot, and a return spring (0.10 N m at rest, 0.24 N m fully squeezed, a 36 degree stroke); its short upper arm, 5 mm above the pivot, pushes (3) a steel gripping plate (20 g) on the rod inside the housing, held back by its spring (5 N, 1 N/mm). (4) The gun's zinc-plated steel plunger rod (0.10 kg, 8 mm thick, 30 cm long) with a 4 cm push plate inside the cradle, 8 cm in front of the back plate, and a D-shaped hook (4.4 cm long, 4.4 cm tall, 1 cm wide) at its back end, 20 to 24.4 cm right of the centre line. (5) The gun's zinc-plated steel thumb release lever on top of the housing, its ribbed pad 3 cm wide, 13 cm above the table, between 0.8 cm right and 1.6 cm left of the centre line. (6) A cardboard tray 10 cm wide and 34 cm long, its middle 17 cm forward and 18 cm left, with two notched cardboard saddles; on them, lying along the table with its nozzle to the left, a new 310 ml cartridge of grey sanitary silicone (0.37 kg): a white polyethylene tube 4.9 cm across and 20.5 cm long (bore 4.6 cm) with a blue and yellow label, its polyethylene piston 4 mm in from the back end, and a translucent nozzle 12 cm long, already cut to a 7 mm opening; its middle 17 cm forward and 17.5 cm left. (7) The white acrylic rim of a bath, 10 cm tall, from 14 to 48 cm forward and from 39 to 43.2 cm left, against (8) a wall of white ceramic tiles (7.5 cm square, grey grout) rising 30 cm from 43.2 cm left. The joint to seal is the corner where the rim's top meets the tiles, from 18.5 to 37.7 cm forward (19.2 cm). The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The gun works as a real smooth-rod gun: squeezing the trigger toward the grip pushes the gripping plate forward (10:1 at 5 cm below the trigger's pivot), and the plate carries the rod forward; let go, the plate slides back along the rod. The rod slides in freely but comes back out only while the release lever is pressed down at least 6 degrees. The rod's push plate pushes the cartridge's piston, which the silicone resists with 150 N. Sealant: the piston's advance times the 46 mm bore (1.66 ml per mm) leaves the nozzle's tip 0.25 s later and is laid along the tip's path; where the bead it makes touches both the rim's top and the tiles (the tip within the bead's radius plus 2 mm of each surface) it is in the joint, shared over the joint's 1 mm lengths it covers. A 1 mm length is sealed when it holds at least 12.6 mm2 of it (a bead at least 4 mm across; a 6 mm bead is 28.3 mm2). Sealant laid anywhere else never counts, and with no squeeze of the trigger there is none. At the end: 1.0 if at least 95% of the joint is sealed with no unsealed stretch longer than 2 mm (its ends included) and the gun is put down (its grip's foot within 2 cm of the table, tilted at most 25 degrees) with both grippers clear of it (each gripper's grip point, between its finger pads, at least 6 cm from its frame, trigger and rod); 0.75 if sealed so but the gun is not put down or a gripper is not clear; 0.5 if at least 50% of the joint is sealed; 0.25 if the gun is loaded: the cartridge seated in the cradle nozzle first (its axis within 8 mm of the cradle's middle sideways and within 1 cm up or down, pointing within 8 degrees of the gun's axis, its shoulder at most 3 cm short of the yoke) with the push plate within 2 mm of its piston; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the gun, its trigger, gripping plate, rod and lever, the cartridge and its piston still. In a real trial: photograph the joint from above with a steel rule along it; the sealed length is where the bead is at least 4 mm wide and wets both the rim and the tile, read off the rule to the millimetre, as is the longest gap; whether the gun is put down and untouched is judged from the video; loaded means the cartridge sits nozzle through the yoke and the rod will not go further in by hand.
reset_notes: Scrape the bead out of the joint, take the cartridge out of the gun and lay a new one on the tray, press the release and set the rod with its plate 8 cm in front of the back plate, and lay the gun back on its grip and rest block.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz). Physical: sprung hinged trigger (10:1), sprung gripping plate, rod, piston. Rules: the plates' friction grip on the smooth rod (a one-way stop kept behind the gripping plate; a hold on the rod unless the lever is down) and the silicone's 150 N resistance (a capped spring moved along the piston). Silicone is not simulated: piston advance x 16.6 cm2 leaves the tip 0.25 s later, drawn as grey rounds. Grip 9 cm long (real about 12).
